title: 📸 Galaxy S27 Ultra may lose its laser autofocus sensor and 3x zoom camera!
body: 📸 Galaxy S27 Ultra may lose its laser autofocus sensor and 3x zoom camera!

Well-known leaker Ice Universe revealed on 24 November that Samsung's upcoming Galaxy S27 Ultra will drop the laser autofocus sensor, the first time Samsung has dropped this sensor in its Ultra phones since it appeared in the Galaxy S21 Ultra in 2021.

The sensor helps the camera focus faster and more accurately, especially in low light, by firing an infrared beam that measures the distance to the subject; Samsung will instead rely, according to the leaker, on an AI-powered focusing technology called AI Focus, with no explanation yet of how it works.

It is not the only missing piece: earlier leaks from the same source suggest the phone will also drop the 10-megapixel 3x optical zoom camera, leaving a single 5x zoom camera, which means the 2027 flagship will carry less camera hardware than its predecessor, the S26 Ultra, relying on cropping from a new 200-megapixel main sensor to cover close zoom levels.

The leaks also revealed a new design with a horizontal camera platform stretching across the width of the phone, similar to the design of recent iPhone Pro models, but — according to the leaker — it is mostly cosmetic, as the right side of it remains almost empty with no real function.

The Galaxy S27 series is expected to launch in early 2027, and Samsung has confirmed none of these details yet, so all of the above is leaks that could change before the official announcement — but one thing confirmed so far is that the S Pen will continue.

Simply put: a premium-priced flagship may lose two pieces of camera hardware at once and replace them with AI; either Samsung is confident in its new alternative, or cutting hardware has become an unstoppable trend.
Would you accept Samsung replacing a real camera component with an untested AI technology?
